mainTopic: Whether אדר is always short, adding a day to אלול for practical needs, and when בית דין may delay or hasten ראש חודש.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: is אדר, the month before ניסן, always 29 days? In a second version, רב נחמן tries to prove from the משנה that witnesses may break שבת for ניסן. The גמרא pushes his proof aside. Then רב כהנא shows from the rest of that משנה that breaking שבת needs a real practical reason, and the view that אדר is always short is refuted. Next, עולא reports that אלול was made full so that ראש השנה would not fall next to שבת. The גמרא explains that this was a favor to hot בבל, so that vegetables would not wilt and the dead would not wait two days for burial. A ברייתא seems to forbid adjusting a month for a need. רבא answers that delaying a month is allowed, but sanctifying it early is not, and רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule about pressuring witnesses fits this. רבי יוחנן's teaching seems to contradict it, and אביי and רבא each answer. The amud ends with רב דימי's reversed version and the start of the question about his reason, which is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: If אדר is always short, why break שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if אדר is always 29 days, the date of ראש חודש ניסן is already known, so why may witnesses break שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say אדר is always short, why do we break שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that אדר is always short. If the date is fixed, there seems to be no need for witnesses to travel on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses may break שבת only when their testimony is truly needed. If אדר is always 29 days, day 30 is automatically ראש חודש ניסן. Their trip would then seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Always short, meaning a 29-day month
We desecrate, meaning we allow breaking שבת
Why?

phrases.english: But if you say it is always short,
phrases.notes: "It" is the month of אדר that comes right before ניסן.

phrases.english: why do we desecrate [שבת]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְעוֹלָם חָסֵר, אַמַּאי מְחַלְּלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first version of רב נחמן's proof from the end of the previous section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that אדר next to ניסן is always 29 days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the date is fixed, the witnesses' testimony is not needed. So why would breaking שבת be allowed?

steps.title: There is a מצוה to sanctify based on seeing the moon
steps.stepSummary: The answer: even when the date is known, the month should be sanctified through witnesses who actually saw the moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a מצוה to sanctify the month based on the sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Witnesses still break שבת because it is a מצוה to sanctify the month through real eyewitness testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the date is not enough. The ideal way to declare ראש חודש is through testimony of people who saw the new moon. That מצוה is important enough to allow breaking שבת for it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to sanctify the new month
Based on the sighting of the moon by witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: Even when a calculation tells us the date, the מצוה is to sanctify ראש חודש through witnesses who saw the moon.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle comes back at the end of the section and is the key to rejecting the second proof.

phrases.english: Because it is a מצוה to sanctify based on the sighting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces an independent reason for breaking שבת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses break שבת only when the date is otherwise unknown.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses break שבת even when the date is known, because sanctifying through sighting is itself a מצוה.

steps.title: Second version: רב נחמן cites the משנה about ניסן and תשרי
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב נחמן quotes the משנה that witnesses break שבת for ניסן and תשרי, and sets it up as a proof that אדר is always short.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב נחמן said, we too learned this in a משנה. Witnesses break שבת for two months, ניסן and תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב נחמן's proof. This line only quotes the source. The argument itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the same משנה as before, but this time it is used as support for the view that אדר is always short. The proof depends on asking which view best explains why breaking שבת is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it, meaning there is a source that supports this
The two months whose ראש חודש is especially important for the holidays

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with steps 1–2. There the משנה looked like a problem for the always-short view. Here the same משנה is used as a proof for it.

phrases.english: Some say: Rav Nachman said,
We too have learned [this] in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים מְחַלְּלִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: For two months they desecrate Shabbat —
for Nisan and for Tishrei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second version of the whole proof.
steps.raayaObject: The view that אדר next to ניסן is always 29 days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that witnesses break שבת for ניסן and תשרי

steps.title: The always-short view explains the משנה
steps.stepSummary: If אדר is always short, breaking שבת makes sense because of the מצוה to sanctify based on sighting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say אדר is always short. That is why we break שבת: because it is a מצוה to sanctify based on the sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן shows that the always-short view fits the משנה well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אדר is always 29 days, day 30 must be ראש חודש ניסן and cannot be moved. So if day 30 is שבת, the witnesses must come that day to fulfill the מצוה of sanctifying by sighting.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well, meaning this view has no problem
For that reason

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is always short —
that is why we desecrate [Shabbat],
because it is a מצוה to sanctify based on the sighting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds the first half of the proof from the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה fits this view because the date cannot be moved

steps.title: If אדר could be full, just add a day
steps.stepSummary: If אדר is sometimes 30 days, the בית דין could make it full and sanctify ניסן the next day, with no need to break שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short, why break שבת? Let the court make it full now and sanctify the new month tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes his proof by showing that the other view cannot explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בית דין may choose between 29 and 30 days, they can avoid breaking שבת by adding a day. Then the witnesses come on Sunday. Since the משנה still allows breaking שבת, it seems the month cannot be lengthened, which means אדר is always short.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes full (30 days), sometimes short (29 days)
Let them make it full by adding a 30th day
Now
Tomorrow

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ זִמְנִין מָלֵא זִמְנִין חָסֵר —
phrases.english: But if you say it is sometimes full and sometimes short —
why do we desecrate [Shabbat]?
Let them make it full now,
phrases.notes: He means: count the שבת as day 30 of אדר instead of as ראש חודש.

phrases.english: and sanctify it tomorrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ זִמְנִין מָלֵא זִמְנִין חָסֵר אַמַּאי מְחַלְּלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the proof: the opposing view cannot explain the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this view, breaking שבת could be avoided by adding a day. So why does the משנה allow it?

steps.title: The משנה means when day 31 falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. When day 30 is שבת, we do add a day, but the משנה is talking about when day 31 is שבת and the month cannot be lengthened any more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If day 30 falls on שבת, that is indeed what we do. What case are we dealing with here? Where day 31 falls on שבת, and it is a מצוה to sanctify based on the sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב נחמן's proof. It explains the משנה as a specific case that fits even the view that אדר can be full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that if day 30 is שבת, the בית דין would add a day and not let witnesses break שבת. But a month can never be longer than 30 days. So when day 31 is שבת, ראש חודש must be that day, and the witnesses break שבת because of the מצוה of sanctifying by sighting. The משנה therefore proves nothing about whether אדר is always short.

keyTerms.meaning: That it happened to fall on
Indeed so, meaning yes, that is what we do
What case are we dealing with here? This narrows the case
The 31st day, counting from the start of אדר

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the משנה fails. Breaking שבת for ניסן can be explained by a case where day 31 falls on שבת. The month cannot be pushed off any further, and the מצוה of sanctifying by sighting applies.
steps.confusionAlert: Day 31 does not mean אדר has 31 days. It means the day after day 30, which must be ראש חודש because no month is longer than 30 days.

phrases.english: If the thirtieth day fell on Shabbat —
indeed so.
Here, what are we dealing with?
Where the thirty-first day fell on Shabbat,
since it is a מצוה to sanctify based on the sighting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאִקְּלַע יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּשַׁבָּת הָכִי נָמֵי. הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 3–5 by narrowing the משנה's case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The משנה fits both views.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה covers a case where adding a day is possible. It actually describes day 31 on שבת, where no further delay is allowed.

steps.title: רב כהנא quotes the rest of the משנה about the time of the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא quotes the next part of the משנה: when the בית המקדש stood, witnesses broke שבת for every month, for the sake of the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא raised an objection: When the בית המקדש was standing, the witnesses would break שבת even for all the months, in order to set the קרבן right.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a new line from the same משנה to push back against the proof that אדר is always short. This line sets up the argument he makes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה said witnesses break שבת only for ניסן and תשרי. Now the continuation says that in the days of the בית המקדש they broke שבת for all twelve months. The reason given there is the קרבן of ראש חודש, not the מצוה of sanctifying by sighting.

keyTerms.meaning: They break (desecrate) שבת
Setting the offering right, so the ראש חודש קרבן is brought on the correct day
The Temple

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection:
When the Temple was standing,
they would break Shabbat even for all of them,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all the months of the year, not just ניסן and תשרי.

phrases.english: because of setting the offering right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the דחיה in step 6 defended the reading, רב כהנא brings a new source against רב נחמן's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's proof (steps 3-4) that אדר is always short, which relied on the מצוה of sanctifying by sighting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה says the breaking of שבת for every month was because of the קרבן. That suggests sighting is not the reason for breaking שבת.

steps.title: So the reason is not the מצוה of sanctifying by sighting
steps.stepSummary: Since the other months were not about the מצוה of sighting, ניסן and תשרי are also not about that מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since for all the other months the reason is not the מצוה to sanctify based on sighting, then for ניסן and תשרי too, the reason is not the מצוה to sanctify based on sighting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא draws a conclusion from the line he quoted. If breaking שבת for the other months had a different reason, the same must be true for ניסן and תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רב נחמן explained the breaking of שבת for ניסן by the מצוה to sanctify through sighting. רב כהנא removes that reason: the משנה shows that breaking שבת depends on a real practical need, not on that מצוה. So ניסן and תשרי also need a practical reason.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that all of them
To sanctify the month based on actual sighting
Also, as well

phrases.english: From the fact that all of them
are not because it is a מצוה
to sanctify based on sighting —
Nisan and Tishrei as well
are not because it is a מצוה
to sanctify based on sighting.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּכוּלְּהוּ לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּמִצְוָה לְקַדֵּשׁ עַל הָרְאִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה line quoted in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the Shabbat-breaking for ניסן and תשרי is not based on the מצוה of sanctifying by sighting
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's statement that in the days of the מקדש they broke שבת for all months because of the קרבן

steps.title: If אדר is always short, why break שבת?
steps.stepSummary: If אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short, breaking שבת makes sense. If it is always short, there is no reason to break שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short; that is why we break שבת. But if you say it is always short, why do we break שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא finishes his attack. Without the מצוה of sighting as a reason, the view that אדר is always short cannot explain the Shabbat-breaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אדר can be 29 or 30 days, nobody knows when ניסן begins until witnesses come, so they have a real reason to break שבת. If אדר is always 29 days, the date of ניסן is already known, and the witnesses' trip serves no practical purpose. Since step 8 removed the מצוה of sighting as a reason, nothing is left to justify breaking שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense if you say (the setup of a 'this works, but that doesn't' challenge)
Full, a 30-day month
Short, a 29-day month
Always

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that it is sometimes full and sometimes short,
for that reason we break Shabbat.
But if you say it is always short,
why do we break Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא זִמְנִין מָלֵא וְזִמְנִין חָסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference of step 8 to the question of whether אדר is always short.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אדר is always short
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the מצוה of sighting is not the reason, only real uncertainty about the date justifies breaking שבת. A fixed 29-day אדר leaves no uncertainty.

steps.title: The challenge stands: a refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares רב כהנא's challenge a full refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion. רב כהנא's question has no answer, so the proof that אדר is always short is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיובתא means the challenge is conclusive and the view it attacks falls. Here the view that falls is רב נחמן's claim in this version that אדר is always short. The conclusion is that אדר can sometimes be 30 days.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the challenged view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, the claim that אדר is always short is refuted. The משנה shows that witnesses break שבת only where there is a real need, and a fixed-length אדר would leave none.

phrases.english: It is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Declares the challenge of step 9 unanswerable.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The view that אדר is always 29 days is refuted; אדר can sometimes be full.

steps.title: עולא reports that אלול was made full
steps.stepSummary: When עולא came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, he reported that the בית דין had added a day to אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came, he said: They made אלול a full month.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. עולא arrives in בבל and reports that this year אלול was given 30 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making אלול full pushes ראש השנה back by one day. This shows the בית דין could lengthen a month on purpose, not only based on when the moon was seen.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
They lengthened it, adding a 30th day
The month before תשרי

phrases.english: When Ulla came, he said:
They made Elul full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion after the refutation closed the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: That year, the בית דין in ארץ ישראל added a day to אלול.

steps.title: עולא: do the Babylonians know the favor we did them?
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the Babylonian scholars should appreciate the favor done for them by lengthening אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Do our Babylonian colleagues know what kindness we did for them!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a comment to his report: lengthening אלול was a favor to the people of בבל. This sets up the גמרא's next question about what that favor was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא presents the extra day in אלול as a deliberate choice that helped people, not just a technical calendar matter. He does not say here what the benefit was. That is left for the גמרא to explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our Babylonian colleagues, the scholars in בבל
A kindness, a favor
With them, for them

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Do our Babylonian colleagues know
what kindness we did for them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא comments on his own report from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding a day to אלול was done as a deliberate benefit for the people of בבל.

steps.title: What is the favor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what benefit comes from adding a day to אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what favor עולא meant when he said the Babylonians should appreciate the extra day in אלול. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a day to אלול moves ראש השנה and יום הכפורים so they do not land right next to שבת. The question is why having two holy days in a row is such a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: a favor, a benefit

phrases.english: What is the benefit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind עולא's statement in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical benefit comes from keeping a יום טוב from falling next to שבת.

steps.title: Two reasons: vegetables or the dead
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the reason is the vegetables. רבי אחא בר חנינא says it is the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: because of the vegetables. רבי אחא בר חנינא said: because of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different reasons why two holy days in a row is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא worries that people would go two days without picking fresh vegetables, so their food would wilt. רבי אחא בר חנינא worries that a body would wait two days for burial and begin to decay.

keyTerms.meaning: vegetables
the dead

phrases.english: עולא said: Because of the vegetables.
phrases.notes: Vegetables could not be picked for two days, and what was picked earlier would wilt.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם מִתַיָּא.
phrases.english: רבי אחא בר חנינא said: Because of the dead.
phrases.notes: A person who died could not be buried for two days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The favor protects either fresh vegetables (עולא) or timely burial of the dead (רבי אחא בר חנינא).

steps.title: What is the difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a case where the two reasons lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to a different ruling. This sets up the search for a test case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons lead to adding a day to אלול in the usual case. The גמרא wants a case where only one of the reasons would apply.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a practical difference between the two reasons in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the vegetables reason and the dead reason give different results.

steps.title: First answer: יום הכפורים on Sunday
steps.stepSummary: If יום הכפורים falls right after שבת, the dead reason says to add a day to אלול. The vegetables reason says there is no need, because fresh vegetables can be brought in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is when יום הכפורים falls right after שבת. The one who says 'because of the dead' would add a day to אלול. The one who says 'because of the vegetables' would not: when does a person need vegetables? In the evening after the fast, and in the evening he can go and bring fresh ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a case where the two reasons split: יום הכפורים on Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A body would still wait from שבת through יום הכפורים, so the dead reason calls for adding a day. Nobody eats on יום הכפורים, though, so vegetables are only needed after the fast ends, and they can be picked fresh then.

keyTerms.meaning: we make it full, we add a day (to אלול)
in the evening
he makes the effort and brings them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: Yom Kippur that falls right after Shabbat.
The one who says 'because of the dead': we add a day.
But the one who says 'because of the vegetables':
When does he need them? In the evening,
and in the evening he makes the effort and brings them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ: יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a first test case to answer step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום הכפורים on Sunday: the dead reason adds a day to אלול; the vegetables reason does not need to.

steps.title: The vegetables view should still care about the dead
steps.stepSummary: Even the one who gives the vegetables reason should add a day to אלול because of the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says 'because of the vegetables,' he should still add a day because of the dead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the case just suggested. Surely nobody would ignore the concern for the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא only gave the vegetables as his reason, but that does not mean he rejects the concern for the dead. If the dead are a real concern in this case, everyone would add the day, so the case shows no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: he should make it full, add a day to it

phrases.english: But according to the one who says 'because of the vegetables,'
let him add a day because of the dead!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם יַרְקַיָּא, לְעַבְּרֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם מִתַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the test case proposed in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the vegetables view would not add a day when יום הכפורים falls on Sunday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The concern for the dead is valid for everyone, so the vegetables view would add a day here as well, and no difference remains.

steps.title: New answer: a יום טוב next to שבת
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a יום טוב right before or after שבת. The vegetables view adds a day to אלול. The dead view does not, because gentiles can bury the dead on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference is a יום טוב next to שבת, either before it or after it. The one who says 'because of the vegetables' adds a day. The one who says 'because of the dead' does not, because the burial can be done by gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the first case and offers a new one, where the dead are not a problem but the vegetables are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a יום טוב, unlike on יום הכפורים, people eat, so wilting vegetables are a real problem and the vegetables view adds a day. Burial on יום טוב can be done by gentiles, so the dead view sees no need to add a day.

keyTerms.meaning: a יום טוב right next to שבת
it can be done by gentiles

steps.confusionAlert: This case flips the first one. Now it is the vegetables view that adds a day to אלול, and the dead view that does not.

phrases.english: Rather, there is a difference between them:
a Festival that is next to Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The יום טוב meant here is ראש השנה.

phrases.english: whether before it or after it.
The one who says 'because of the vegetables': we add a day,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם מִתַיָּא — אֶפְשָׁר בְּעַמְמֵי.
phrases.english: and the one who says 'because of the dead': it is possible through gentiles.
phrases.notes: On יום טוב, gentiles can take care of the burial, so there is no need to make אלול longer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ יוֹם טוֹב הַסָּמוּךְ לַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case that step 17 knocked down with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the test case with a different one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was thought to be יום הכפורים on Sunday.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is a יום טוב next to שבת, where the dead are not a problem (gentiles can bury them) but the vegetables are.

steps.title: The dead view should still care about the vegetables
steps.stepSummary: Even the one who gives the dead reason should add a day to אלול because of the vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says 'because of the dead,' he should still add a day because of the vegetables!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new case in the same way as before. Why would the dead view ignore the vegetables?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors the challenge in step 17. If wilting vegetables are a real problem on this יום טוב, everyone should add the day, and the difference disappears again.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says 'because of the dead,'
let him add a day because of the vegetables!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם מִתַיָּא, לְעַבְּרֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם יַרְקַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new case from step 18, in the same way step 17 challenged step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dead view would not add a day when a יום טוב is next to שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vegetables concern is valid for everyone, so the dead view should add a day as well.

steps.title: Wilted vegetables can be revived in hot water
steps.stepSummary: The dead view does not worry about the vegetables, because wilted vegetables can be freshened in hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible with hot water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for the dead view, the vegetables problem has an easy fix, so it does not justify adding a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking wilted vegetables in hot water brings back their freshness, so the dead view does not see this as a real loss. That keeps the difference alive: in the case of a יום טוב next to שבת, only the vegetables view adds a day to אלול.

keyTerms.meaning: hot water

steps.whatToRemember: Final practical difference: when a יום טוב falls next to שבת, עולא (vegetables) adds a day to אלול. רבי אחא בר חנינא (the dead) does not, because gentiles can bury the dead and wilted vegetables can be revived in hot water.

phrases.english: It is possible with hot water.
phrases.notes: Soaking the wilted vegetables in hot water makes them fresh again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19 and keeps the case from step 18 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the competing concern can be solved another way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vegetables problem should force even the dead view to add a day.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot water revives wilted vegetables, so the dead view has no need to add a day.

steps.title: Why only a benefit for בבל?
steps.stepSummary: If the extra day in אלול helps with vegetables and the dead, it should help people in ארץ ישראל too, not just in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why is it different for us? It should help them too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's wording. He said the extra day in אלול was a favor to 'us' in בבל, but the reasons given apply to people in ארץ ישראל as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons, the vegetables and the dead, are about problems when a יום טוב falls right next to שבת. Those problems seem to exist everywhere. So why single out בבל?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What is the difference?
For us (the people of בבל)
For them (the people of ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: If so, what is different for us?
phrases.notes: 'Us' means the people of בבל, whom עולא said were helped by the extra day in אלול.

phrases.english: Even for them as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both reasons have been explained, the גמרא asks why עולא said the benefit was only for בבל.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's statement that the extra day was a favor to the people of בבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reasons (vegetables and the dead) apply in every place, so the benefit should not be limited to בבל.

steps.title: בבל is hot, ארץ ישראל is not
steps.stepSummary: In hot בבל, vegetables wilt and the dead decay quickly. In ארץ ישראל the weather is milder, so two days in a row is not a real problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: For us, the weather is hot. For them, the weather is not hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the climate is different. Heat makes the two-day problem serious in בבל but not in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasons are the same, but how serious they are depends on the weather. In heat, vegetables wilt and a body decays fast, so two days without picking fresh vegetables or burying the dead is hard. In a cooler place things can wait two days.

keyTerms.meaning: Hot, steamy
Literally 'the world'; here, the weather

phrases.english: For us, the weather is hot;
for them, the weather is not hot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by real-world conditions (climate)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The benefit of the extra day should be the same everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: The benefit matters mostly in hot בבל, where food and bodies spoil quickly.
steps.whatToRemember: Adding a day to אלול keeps ראש השנה from falling right next to שבת. This helps with the vegetables and the dead, and that help matters most in a hot place like בבל.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to forbid changing the month for a need
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא says a month cannot be adjusted for a need the way a year can, because the moon must be seen and then sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבה בר שמואל taught: One might think that just as we add a month to the year for a need, we also add a day to a month for a need. So the verse says, 'This month shall be to you the head of months': when you see it like this, sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the whole idea of adding a day to אלול for practical reasons. It brings a ברייתא that seems to forbid this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we assumed בית דין may delay a month for a practical need. The ברייתא says a year may be lengthened for a need, but a month may not. The month depends on seeing the moon: 'see it and sanctify.' That seems to contradict what was said before.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (opens a challenge)
But didn't he teach (in a ברייתא)?
Make longer: add a month to a year or a day to a month
For a need, for a practical reason
See it like this, and sanctify

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of מְעַבְּרִין: making a YEAR longer by a month, and making a MONTH longer by a day. The ברייתא seems to allow the first and forbid the second.

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't רבה בר שמואל teach:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה לְצוֹרֶךְ,
phrases.english: One might think that just as we add to the year for a need,
so too we add to the month for a need?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״הַחֹדֶשׁ הַזֶּה לָכֶם רֹאשׁ חֳדָשִׁים״
phrases.english: So the verse says: 'This month shall be to you the head of months'
— when it is like this, see it and sanctify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of adding a day to אלול to whether adding a day to a month for a need is allowed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that בית דין may add a day to a month (like אלול) for a practical need
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the month follows the sighting of the moon and cannot be adjusted for a need, unlike the year.

steps.title: רבא: delaying is different from sanctifying early
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there is no contradiction. Delaying the month is allowed, but declaring it early is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is not difficult. Here it is about making the month longer; there it is about sanctifying it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by showing that the two sources are talking about two different actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Making it longer' (לעברו) means delaying ראש חודש by a day even though the moon was seen. That is allowed for a need. 'Sanctifying it' (לקדשו) means declaring ראש חודש early, before the moon is seen. That is what the ברייתא forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here ... there (two different cases)
To make it longer (delay the month)
To sanctify it (declare ראש חודש)

phrases.english: רבא said: It is not difficult:
Here it is about making it longer; there it is about sanctifying it.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our case of adding a day to אלול; 'there' is the ברייתא, which is about sanctifying early.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לְעַבְּרוֹ, כָּאן לְקַדְּשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two different actions (delaying vs. sanctifying early)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids any change to the month for a need.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only declaring ראש חודש early is forbidden; delaying it for a need is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule: בית דין can make a month longer for a need, but can never make ראש חודש before the moon is seen.

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא again: just as year and month may be lengthened for a need, one might think a month may be sanctified early for a need. The verse teaches no.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: One might think that just as we lengthen the year and the month for a need, we also sanctify the month for a need. So the verse says, 'This month shall be to you': when you see it like this, sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now reads the ברייתא in a way that fits his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, the ברייתא agrees that both a year and a month can be lengthened for a need. Its new point is about the opposite move: sanctifying the month early, before the moon appears. The verse 'see it and sanctify' blocks only that.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it means
We sanctify (declare ראש חודש)

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה וְאֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ לְצוֹרֶךְ,
phrases.english: One might think that just as we lengthen the year and the month for a need,
so too we sanctify the month for a need —
phrases.notes: He means sanctifying it early, on the thirtieth day, before the moon was seen.

phrases.english: so the verse says: 'This month shall be to you' —
when it is like this, see it and sanctify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by showing how to read the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says a month may not be lengthened for a need.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows lengthening and forbids only sanctifying early.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי on pressuring witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says בית דין may pressure witnesses so as to delay the month, but not so as to make ראש חודש early. This fits רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי יהושע בן לוי said: We may pressure the witnesses about a moon that was seen on time, in order to make the month longer. But we may not pressure the witnesses about a moon that was not seen on time, in order to sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי that matches רבא's difference between delaying and declaring early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the moon was seen on time, בית דין may press the witnesses hard so their testimony fails, and the month gets an extra day. This is delaying, which is allowed. But they may not push witnesses to claim they saw a moon that was not seen, in order to make ראש חודש early. This is the same line רבא drew.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is like that (a matching teaching)
Pressure, intimidate (through tough questioning)
Witnesses
In its time (on the thirtieth day)

steps.whatToRemember: Main rule: בית דין may make a month longer for a need, even by pressing the witnesses. But it may never make ראש חודש before the moon is really seen.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And this is like what רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
We may pressure the witnesses
about a moon that was seen in its time — in order to make the month longer;
phrases.notes: 'In its time' means on the thirtieth day. Pushing the testimony aside delays ראש חודש to the next day.

phrases.english: but we may not pressure the witnesses

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאָה בִּזְמַנּוֹ — לְקַדְּשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: about a moon that was not seen in its time — in order to sanctify it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's distinction with a matching ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that delaying a month is allowed but sanctifying early is not
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling about pressuring witnesses on the new moon

steps.title: רבי יוחנן allowed pressuring witnesses to make the month early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule from Step 26 with a message from רבי יהודה נשיאה. He reports that רבי יוחנן taught that witnesses may be pressured to say they saw the moon, so the month can be sanctified early.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? רבי יהודה נשיאה sent a message to רבי אמי: 'Know that all his life רבי יוחנן taught us that we may pressure witnesses about a moon that was not seen in its time, so that the month can be sanctified. Even though they did not see it, they should say: We saw it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that ראש חודש may be delayed but not made early. It brings רבי יוחנן, who allowed exactly the thing that rule forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said בית דין may pressure witnesses only to delay the month. רבי יוחנן says בית דין may pressure witnesses to claim they saw a moon they did not see, so the month starts on the 30th day instead of the 31st. That is making the month early, which directly clashes with רבא and רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word that signals a challenge
We pressure or threaten
Seen in its proper time (on the 30th day)
To sanctify it (to declare ראש חודש)
The נשיא (head of the court) who sent the message

steps.confusionAlert: This is not permission to lie for its own sake. The point is that בית דין can push the calendar so ראש חודש falls on the 30th day for a communal need, even without a real sighting.

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yehuda Nesia send a message to Rabbi Ami:
Be aware

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָיָה מְלַמְּדֵנוּ:
phrases.english: that all the days of Rabbi Yochanan he would teach us:
We may pressure the witnesses
about a new moon that was not seen in its proper time
in order to sanctify it;
phrases.notes: He means sanctifying the month on the 30th day, which is earlier than it would otherwise be.

phrases.english: even though they did not see it,
they should say "We saw it"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule that Step 26 had just supported
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רבא and רבי יהושע בן לוי that the month may be delayed but not made early
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן allowed pressuring witnesses so the month starts early, which is exactly what that rule forbids

steps.title: אביי: ניסן and תשרי are different from the other months
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי יוחנן's teaching applies to ניסן and תשרי, while the rule against making the month early applies to the other months.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no contradiction. This teaching is about ניסן and תשרי, and that teaching is about the other months.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction by saying each teaching deals with different months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניסן and תשרי contain the major holidays, so getting their dates right is important enough to allow making the month early. In the other months there is no such need, so the month may only be delayed, never made early.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
The months with פסח and the fall holidays
The other months

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult:
this is in Nisan and Tishrei,
phrases.notes: This first 'this' is רבי יוחנן's teaching, which allows making the month early.

phrases.english: that is in the other months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings seemed to give opposite rules about making the month early
steps.terutzMaskana: Making the month early is allowed in ניסן and תשרי for the holidays, but not in other months

steps.title: רבא: רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא follows אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל, which said months cannot be adjusted for a need, follows the opinion of אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What רבה בר שמואל taught is the opinion of אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction a different way. The ברייתא that forbade adjusting the month is only one opinion, and רבי יוחנן did not follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 23) the ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל seemed to forbid changing months for a need. רבא now labels it as the view of אחרים, who hold the months follow a fixed pattern. The other חכמים allow adjustments, so רבי יוחנן can follow them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name for a תנא whose opinion is quoted

phrases.english: Rava said:
That which Rabba bar Shmuel taught
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from Step 23, that a month cannot be adjusted for a need.

phrases.english: is the opinion of Acherim.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אֲחֵרִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer, different from אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning a source to a minority opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be the accepted rule against adjusting months
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects only אחרים; the חכמים allow adjustments, so רבי יוחנן stands

steps.title: אחרים: holidays move only four days each year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows where אחרים's view comes from. They say שבועות and ראש השנה move only four weekdays from one year to the next, or five in a leap year, which means the months follow a fixed pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: אחרים say: Between עצרת of one year and עצרת of the next, and between ראש השנה of one year and ראש השנה of the next, there are only four days. If it was a leap year, there are five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא of אחרים to support רבא's claim that they hold the months never change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the holiday always moves exactly four weekdays, the year must always be the same length. That only works if the months are fixed (alternating full and short) and בית דין never adds or removes a day. So אחרים are the ones who would say months cannot be adjusted for a need.

keyTerms.meaning: שבועות
A leap year (with an extra month)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אחרים the calendar is fixed, so holidays shift by exactly four days a year. The חכמים disagree and let בית דין adjust months.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Acherim say:
There is no difference between Atzeret and Atzeret

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּין רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: and no difference between Rosh HaShana and Rosh HaShana
except four days alone.
phrases.notes: Four days of the week: if ראש השנה is on Monday this year, next year it falls on Friday.

phrases.english: And if it was a leap year, five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim in Step 29
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that אחרים hold the months cannot be adjusted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אחרים about the fixed four-day shift of the holidays

steps.title: רב דימי teaches the rule about pressuring witnesses in reverse
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי from נהרדעא teaches the rule about pressuring witnesses the opposite way. Witnesses may be pressured so the month starts early, but not so the month is delayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא taught it the opposite way: We may pressure the witnesses about a moon not seen in its time, in order to sanctify the month. But we may not pressure the witnesses about a moon seen in its time, in order to add a day to the month.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a reversed version of the teaching from Step 26. In his version it matches רבי יוחנן instead of contradicting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 26 רבי יהושע בן לוי allowed pressure only to delay the month. רב דימי's version says the reverse: pressure is allowed only to make the month early. This removes the contradiction with רבי יוחנן, but it now goes against רבא's rule from Step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it the opposite way
To make it full (add a 30th day to the month)

steps.confusionAlert: Here לעברו means adding a day to the month, not adding a month to the year.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi from Neharde'a teaches it the opposite way:
phrases.notes: He is reversing the teaching about pressuring witnesses from Step 26.

phrases.english: We may pressure the witnesses

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַחֹדֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאָה בִּזְמַנּוֹ — לְקַדְּשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: about a moon that was not seen in its time, in order to sanctify it,
but we may not pressure the witnesses
about a moon that was seen in its time, in order to make the month full.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reversed version of Step 26 that matches רבי יוחנן (Step 27)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses may be pressured so the month is sanctified early, but not so the month is made full (delayed)
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the disagreement is partly about the correct wording of the teaching. That changes which direction of calendar change בית דין may push.

steps.title: Asking for the reason behind רב דימי's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב דימי allows pressuring witnesses only in one direction, to start the month early and not to delay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב דימי's rule from the previous step. This line is setting up the next move, where the גמרא will explain his logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי allowed pressuring witnesses to say they saw the moon, which starts the month early. He did not allow pressuring them to stay quiet, which would delay the month. The גמרא wants to know why one kind of pressure is allowed and the other is not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A standard way the גמרא asks for the logic behind a ruling.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב דימי's one-sided rule about pressuring witnesses, taught in Step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic for why witnesses may be pressured so the month starts early, but not so it is delayed.
